text:
A teenage boy stabbed a 14-year-old girl 55 times after the pair met up in a park near her home, a jury has heard.
The body of Lilly Jones was found two days later in a wooded area about 500 metres from her home in south Wales, the court was told.
Lilly and the boy, also 14, had been messaging each other for several months having developed “some kind of relationship” and arranged to meet on the evening she was killed, the court heard.
Lilly learned the boy was also “in a relationship” with another girl and the two teenage girls had planned to confront him, the jury heard.
Anna Pope KC, prosecuting, said: “This case is about the tragic death of Lilly Jones who in June this year had just turned 14. At around 6.30pm on Saturday 20 June she went out, telling her dad she was popping out for a bit. She never came home.”
The police were contacted and a missing person investigation began. Lilly was found dead two days after meeting up with the boy, the jury heard, with stab wounds on her neck, back and chest.
“The missing person inquiry turned into a murder inquiry,” Pope said.
The boy and Lilly were seen on CCTV together at about 6.50pm on the evening she went missing, Newport crown court heard.
Pope said: “Police quickly identified that the last person to see Lilly alive was the boy.”
When he was first approached by police, the defendant told them he had been due to meet up with Lilly but she did not turn up. After being shown the CCTV footage, he said he had been with her for 15 minutes before he left her, the court heard.
Pope said: “We say Lilly did not meet up with anyone else that night. We say that the boy was the last person to see her alive. We say that he was the person who murdered Lilly and then left her in the woods, either dying or already dead.”
The court heard the boy and Lilly began to “take an interest” in each other in March when Lilly was 13.
Pope said Lilly later learned the boy was also “in some sort of relationship” with another girl. Jurors were told Lilly and the other girl formed a friendship and had planned to confront the boy.
The court was told the boy’s DNA was found under Lilly’s nails, from where she had scratched him. A knife was recovered from the boy’s bedroom that could be scientifically linked to Lilly, jurors heard. Her phone was never discovered.
Pope said Lilly, from the town of Blaina, enjoyed cosplay, Pokémon and was in regular contact with her friends in school. The prosecutor said Lily had been shopping with her father for Pokémon cards on the day she was attacked.
In opening remarks to the jury, Mrs Justice Stacey said: “The boy says it was not him who did it but it was someone else she met after he left her in the park. The death of a teenage girl, especially in these circumstances is very distressing, and the fact a 14-year-old boy has been accused of her murder is also very distressing.”
The defendant, who cannot be named, denies murder. The trial continues.
